before.abstract_text: Risk limits on dealer positions concern the largest magnitude reached before a review horizon ends, rather than the position at its endpoint. We compare historical and conditional quantile forecasts of sampled absolute-position peaks for an FX market maker and weekly primary-dealer position aggregates. Simple historical rules prove difficult to beat. Long-history FX regression changes matched loss by -14.77% and -16.62% in the later and earlier periods. Its later advantage survives the evaluated finite delayed coverage correction. Before correction, however, regression breaches more frequently, while its ranking against a shorter-history rolling rule changes across periods. After stronger regularization, regression still loses 34 of 48 additional-panel comparisons. We formalize the known-floor target and apply a classical endpoint-to-peak bound under explicit assumptions. The results support joint validation of accuracy, breach behavior, and stability across reference rules, periods, and related series.
changes_by_sentences: Long-history FX regression changes matched loss by -14.77% and -16.62% in the later and earlier periods
Against a historical headroom rule with the same history, its later-period loss changes by -14.77%
The earlier-period matched comparison changes loss by -16.62%, and the evaluated coverage correction preserves the later advantage
Wrapped regression changes mean loss by -15.00% against the wrapped historical reference on their common evaluation grid
The fixed mean combination instead changes that loss by 2.77%, and the headroom quantile recursion is also worse than the reference in that primary context
